[head=1][color=#ff6b6b]USE A DEDICATED CHARACTER[/color][/head]
[head=3]Make a character that [italic]only[/italic] responds to faxes. It must not be used for any other role.[/head]
# Fax Responder You answer faxes sent to your fax machine on behalf of the [bold]RMC14 admin team[/bold], so you are held to the highest standards.
[bold][color=#ff6b6b]Key rules[/color][/bold] - Breaking these guidelines can lose you the role, or in extreme cases, earn a server ban. - You [bold]cannot[/bold] authorize ERTs or PMC deployments. Always AHELP. - [bold]Never[/bold] transmit on your radio. It is listen-only. - You are [bold]epiphenomenal[/bold]: you never influence the outcome or decisions of the round.
## Your Role You are a fax [bold]responder[/bold]. Probing a little to let players know you're there is fine, but work mostly on a [bold]"Yes, therefore"[/bold] basis.
[color=#ffcc66]This is not a very active role.[/color] Don't expect to regularly fax multiple departments; that isn't your purpose.
Your goal is to [bold]enhance the roleplay of players in the round[/bold], not to force your own story onto it. Many CLs and Correspondents join with a plan for how they want to roleplay, and being told to do something else can be jarring.
- Setting tasks or missions is fine, but [bold]check first[/bold] that the player is willing, [bold]and[/bold] keep them comparable to the [bold]Available Faxes[/bold] examples below. - Players can misread what you say (and sometimes self antag). Choose your words carefully. - If you don't know the person you're faxing, be precise and spell things out.
[bold][color=#7ee29a]Do[/color][/bold]
[bold][color=#ff6b6b]Don't[/color][/bold]
- Alert staff to anything that may need oversight, like a CO arrest or RP standard breaches. - Keep faxes professional and true to who you represent. - Use the supplied document formats, so every responder feels consistent. - Embody your faction. Quirks are fine, but you are of the faction first. - Contact admins about anything ambiguous or tangential.
- Transmit on your radio, ever. - Call anyone without an [bold]exceptional[/bold] reason. - Answer calls you weren't expecting. - Disrupt the round or push players to antag. - Authorize any ERT without an admin. (You need their help anyway.)
## Access to the Role Requires [bold]75+ hours as Corporate Liaison[/bold]. You should consistently show high-quality roleplay and strong spelling, grammar and formatting.
[color=#ff6b6b][bold]Abusing the role or ignoring these rules will result in an immediate roleban. If in doubt, contact an admin.[/bold][/color]
## What Can I Do? You hold real authority, so make measured decisions. Be creative and avoid repeating the same requests, so it stays fun for everyone involved.
Play to players' RP strengths and follow the [bold]golden map[/bold]: - [bold]1.[/bold] Make contact with the related parties, or receive a fax to respond to. - [bold]2.[/bold] Establish the scenario at play. - [bold]3. Therefore[/bold], you or the player decide on an action. - [bold]4. But[/bold], that action comes with a caveat. - [bold]5. Therefore[/bold], pivot, or escalate the severity. - [bold]6.[/bold] ...and so on.
### General Guidelines - Respond to relevant faxes addressed to your faction. - Coordinate with other responders if a message is misdirected. - Roleplay with other responders by phone or fax. - Decide whether to report suspicious activity to UNMC Command, based on your faction's interests. - Assume anyone trying to betray the UNMC is [bold]not[/bold] staff-approved, and discourage it unless told otherwise. - Request and respond to status reports from your faction's personnel.
## Available Faxes
### Weston-Yamada - Give the Corporate Liaison non-antagonistic objectives. - Have them collect materials or data from the colony. (They need permission from research staff, so it isn't antagonistic to the UNMC.) - Order interviews with survivors or station personnel. - Request NDAs from involved parties. - Help newer players with worldbuilding. - Provide remote legal support. - [color=#ff6b6b]You may [bold]not[/bold] authorize a WeYa PMC deployment. Always AHELP such requests.[/color]
### Free Press - Have the Correspondent investigate rumors of colonial instability or corporate negligence. - Have them document survivors' living conditions or morale. - Request a feature story about anything that's happened in the round. - Have them run "Man on the Street" interviews with low-ranking marines about the battle. - [color=#ff6b6b]You may [bold]not[/bold] give objectives that break Marine Law, such as stealing items or classified documents.[/color]
## Fax Responder Types
[bold][color=#7ee29a]Available[/color][/bold]
[bold][color=#ffcc66]Admin only[/color][/bold]
- Weston-Yamada - Free Press
- UNMC High Command - UNMC Provost Office - Colonial Marshal Bureau - SPP High Command - TSE Imperial Command - CLF Command
## Admin-Only Faxes These are only played by the admin team.
### UNMC High Command - You are [bold]not[/bold] a Provost representative. Avoid appeals and Marine Law unless directed, and [bold]defer[/bold] to an active Provost responder or Inspector on legal matters.
### UNMC Provost Office - Respond to properly written and formatted appeal requests. - CLF members permanently confined for allegiance [bold]cannot[/bold] be released without [bold]explicit[/bold] staff approval, and the staff member should send that fax themselves. They are usually held "until the end of the operation". - Approve or deny CO arrest orders [bold]only if no staff are online[/bold]. Always AHELP first. - Authorize transfers of marines to Colonial Marshal custody for black market investigations.
### SPP / TSE / CLF - Outside staff-led events, these factions rarely (if ever) receive faxes. - Report any fax about betraying the UNMC or overt antagonism to staff via [bold]AHELP[/bold] immediately. You may keep it from other responders or CIC in character, but [bold]never[/bold] from staff. - Usually leave these faxes unanswered unless a staff-run event involving your faction is active. Check with an admin first.
